chunks: And if the ruled gain sway over their ruler,
or the ruler oppresses the ruled, then difference crops up in every word there,
and the signs of oppression appear,
and the paths of the Sunnah are forsaken,
then desires are acted upon, and the rulings are discarded,
and diseases of the souls become numerous,
so there is no hesitation in disregarding even a great right that is abandoned,
nor in committing a great wrong that is done!
In such circumstances, the virtuous are humiliated while the vicious are honoured, and there are serious chastisements from Allāh, the Glorified, onto the people.
ai.seo_question: What are the signs of injustice in governance according to Imam Ali in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali identifies this reciprocal breakdown as the onset of 'Ikhtilaf al-Kalimah' (divergence of discourse), a critical state where administrative injustice corrupts religious practice and leads to the widespread neglect of Sunnah. This passage is foundational in Shia political theology for understanding how societal decay begins with the ruler's failure to uphold justice, resulting in the humiliation of the righteous and the elevation of the wicked.

en.sayed-ali-raza: But if the ruled gain sway over the ruler, or the ruler oppresses the ruled, then difference crops up in every word, signs of oppression appear, mischief enters religion and the ways of the sunnah are forsaken.

Then desires are acted upon, the commands (of religion) are discarded, diseases of the spirit become numerous and there is no hesitation in disregarding even great rights, nor in committing big wrongs.
In such circumstances, the virtuous are humiliated while the vicious are honoured, and there are serious chastisements from Allāh, the Glorified, onto the people.
